cards.explanation: The harvest turns out just like what each one sowed. Paul says, "Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously." The harvest follows the seed, friends. Plant a pinch, get a pinch. Plant a LOT, and the field notices.

The answer is False. Paul says each one should give what he has decided in his heart, "…not out of regret or compulsion." That's his instruction, friends: no pressure and no regret. The choice starts in the heart.
God loves a cheerful giver. Paul says, "For God loves a cheerful giver." Cheerful is the word he picks, friends. That's the kind of giver Paul points to when he says to give from the heart.

They'll abound in every good work. Paul says God is able to make all grace abound, "…so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work." Listen to all those alls, friends. It's a LOT of all.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever." The gifts go to the poor. And Paul says it's "written," so he's leaning on Scripture here.

The answer is False. Paul says God "…will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness." The seed store grows, and so does the harvest. Same size is not in this letter, bakers.
The word is righteousness. Paul says God "…will increase the harvest of your righteousness." Seed goes in, and a harvest of righteousness comes out, friends. That's the kind of crop Paul has in mind.
The word is thanksgiving. Paul says "…through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God." The generosity goes out, bakers, and the thanks go up to God.

They'll glorify God for the Corinthians' obedience to the gospel. Paul says the saints "…will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution…" So the gift proves something, friends. It shows an obedient confession of the gospel.
